summary.text: Maria Elvira Salazar is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 27th District. A Miami native and the daughter of Cuban exiles, she spent decades as a Spanish-language television journalist before losing the 2018 race for the seat, winning it in 2020 and taking office in 2021. She is seeking a third re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Miami, Florida, in 1961; her official biography says she was born in Little Havana, the daughter of Cuban exiles.
Studied at the Deerborne School of Coral Gables and graduated from Miami Dade College, according to her official biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree in communications from the University of Miami (1983) and a master's in public administration from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government (1995).

Worked as a television journalist, reporter and news anchor, starting at age 22. Her official biography lists Telemundo, Univision, AmericaTeve, MegaTV and CNN en Español, and says she is a five-time Emmy Award winner who interviewed Fidel Castro.
Ran for the 27th District in 2018 and lost the general election; ran again in 2020 and defeated incumbent Donna Shalala, taking office in 2021. She won re-election in 2022.
Serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and chaired its Western Hemisphere subcommittee in the 2023-2024 Congress.
Lives in Coral Gables with her two daughters, according to her official biography.
